newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol prospects seen bright ahead of offer.
newsitem.headline: Repsol prospects seen bright ahead of offer.

text.p: Results from Spain's Repsol in 1996 show that despite a difficult year in 1996 the energy group's future looks bright, analysts said on Thursday.
Current share price weakness was attributed to mainly technical factors ahead of the sale of the goverment's last 10 percent stake in the energy group, which is expected to go well.

"Repsol is a stock that most fund managers quite like and tend to hold. But there's an issue coming up and it's bound to see weakness in the shares on the prospect of more supply," said an analyst who requested anonymity.
But this should draw more investors.
"It's good for the firm in a way because price weakness basically guarantees the success of the issue," he added.

The government plans to sell its remaining stake in Repsol after the privatisation of Telefonica, which ends on February 18. It may be approved as soon as the end of January, according to state holding group SEPI.
Underlying sentiment towards Repsol is still positive and growth should be strong in 1997, analysts said.
Weakness in the chemicals division and hefty investment necessary for new Latin American buys impacted profits in 1996, which rose just 1.1 percent to 119.01 billion pesetas.

Operating profit fell to 197.23 billion pesetas from 212.50 in 1995. Despite an exceptionally strong increase in results for the exploration and production division, poor chemical results weighed on profits, a Spanish analyst said.

"Refining and marketing is doing better-than-expected, the gas division is basically in line, exploration and production is performing very well indeed but even the chemicals unit has seen a slight recovery," he said.
He forecast a rise in net profit to 130 billion pesetas in 1997, in line with the market consensus for a 9.1 percent rise in net profit to 131.5 billion this year.
Selling ahead of the placement has put pressure on the share price recently.

"For some time there's been a very big sell order, probably from an American fund that is either switching or reducing its stake before subscribing to the new offer. It's more noticeable because (trading) volumes are thinner," said a trader.
Another trader was predicting a pick-up in the share price.
"We think that Repsol's fall in fundamentally linked to its excellent performance in recent months and reflects profit-taking, but we think the correction should be close to ending," the trader said.
At 1440 GMT Repsol was down 100 pesetas, 1.76 percent, to 5,570, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares was up 0.28 percent to 5,294.61.
Since the Popular Party came into government last year, it has set about privatising the remaining partially state-owned giants, so far with huge success. Repsol should be no exception.
A 3.8 percent stake in Gas Natural in December -around three times oversubscribed-- was followed by its last 20.9 percent in Telefonica, proving to be extremely popular with small shareholders.
There are also upcoming sales of 66 percent of Endesa, the privatisation of second telephone operator Retevision, tobacco group Tabacalera and airport retail managers Aldeasa.
